rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the majority narrow and institutional, grounding reversal in the absence of a specific, duty-imposing source of law under Mitchell II and the practical risk that any mandatory “planning/secure water” injunction would collide with the Arizona v. California decree framework. Separate writings are most likely from Gorsuch (to emphasize treaty/trust principles while agreeing no enforceable duty is pleaded) and Sotomayor (dissenting to argue for cabined, process-only relief at the pleading stage).
